correctness.rationale: Full Fourier intensity equality is equality of every aperiodic autocorrelation by trigonometric coefficient uniqueness; coordinate magnitudes give common support and real relative signs. Normalize the signs at the left endpoint; the largest lag then forces agreement at the right endpoint. Each positive lag of the cross-sign pairs must have vanishing sum of products, so none may be a singleton. For three sites an interior flip forces equal gaps and opposite endpoints, yielding minus the reflected sequence. For four sites one interior flip has three cross distances that cannot all coincide. With both flipped and consecutive gaps a,b,c, the only repeated-pair partition of a,a+b,b+c,c permitted by b>0 is a=c and a+b=b+c. Then the two equations are A0*A1+A2*A3=0 and A0*A2+A1*A3=0. Nonzero amplitudes give A3=A0 and A2=-A1 or A3=-A0 and A2=A1, exactly the two signed reflections. Support sizes zero through two are trivial. For sharpness the reversal of 1+tz-z^2 has the same unit-circle modulus; multiplying both factors by 1+uz^2 gives precisely the claimed coefficients. Parameter exclusions make every coefficient nonzero, the matching linear and opposite constant coefficients exclude a global sign, and the unequal endpoint magnitudes exclude the only possible reflection of the common finite support. Inspected the frozen checker; its tests are finite supplementary checks, not the proof for arbitrary real values or gaps.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the sharp five-site threshold for all real finite sequences on Z with both magnitude data, up to signed reflection as well as global sign. Neither the general Fourier-only characterization nor the inspected four-consecutive-tap and sampled-real-line results give this sharp universal two-data conclusion. The factor reversal itself is classical.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased real sparse two-data classification is not excluded.
No priority claim is made for autocorrelation, zero flips or consecutive complex-tap classifications.
